messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: comparing models using waic
parts:
Hi,

I think it is a very simple question but how to compare two different models for the same data using waic when response for one model is scaled (a drastically simplified example):

    for (i in 1 : N) {
         log_lik [i] <- lognormal_log (response [i], input [i], sigma);
    }

and

    for (i in 1 : N) {
        response_scaled [i] <- response [i] / input [i];
         log_lik [i] <- lognormal_log (response_scaled [i], input [i], sigma);
    }

Thanks for any advice,
Linas

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] comparing models using waic
parts:
Hi—As long as the data haven’t changed, you can compute the loglikelihood of the original data points and it should all work.  I think the key is that ultimately you are modeling the data themselves, not the transformed or combined data.
A

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] comparing models using waic
parts:
Hi!

Not sure if I understand Andrew. Assume we have data y and some model for it. Let´s say we have two non-linear transforms f and g which we believe does some good to the data in terms of whatever (better variance structure or so) - but I am not sure if I want to model f(y) or g(y). Hence, in the Stan model I then write either

log_lik [i] <- normal_log (g(y[i]), pred[i], sigma);

or

log_lik [i] <- normal_log (f(y[i]), pred[i], sigma);

to compare the model with f and g respectively (each model is executed independently from the other one).

To my understanding this is how it has to be done, but it feels certainly a bit odd to compare the point-wise log-density based on different data effectively. However, this is the best one can do in this case as such a model lacks a link function. Right? I am asking because in such a scenario, one does not calculate the loglikelihood on the original data, but rather the transformed one - this is the part which confused me in your response.

Best,
Sebastian

messages.author: 20758fda448fdbda
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] comparing models using waic
parts:
Sebastian, if I understand you correctly, you are modifying the raw data to get a better fit. However, once the model is run, the parameters can be restated to be on the "data scale," and as the data is the same, the WAICs calculated by using the different sets of parameters rescaled back to the data ON the same data are now comparable.

Avi
